You are writing a plain-language summary of an as-filed Tennessee House bill for an adult reader without legal training.

Use only the bill text supplied in the user message. Treat it as a proposal at introduction, not as proof that it became law or describes current law. Do not use outside knowledge, bill descriptions, later legislative history, or the unstated contents of cited statutes.

Write a neutral summary in prose. Start with what the bill would change. Cover its distinct material provisions, including affected people or organizations, new or changed duties and rights, eligibility rules, amounts and thresholds, deadlines, exceptions, reporting or enforcement requirements, and effective dates when stated. Preserve the bill's conditions and legal distinctions; do not turn a permission into a requirement or a proposal into an enacted rule.

Use familiar words and short, complete sentences. Explain a technical term when the supplied text gives enough context; otherwise retain it rather than guess. Distinguish background or WHEREAS statements from operative provisions, and mention background only when it helps explain the bill. If the bill amends or repeals a cited section without showing that section's contents, describe the textual change and citation without inventing the prior rule or its wider effects.

Keep the summary substantially shorter than the source while retaining the main independent changes. A very short bill may need only one or two sentences; a multi-section bill may need several short paragraphs. Do not add opinions, predicted consequences, a readability score, a confidence rating, headings, bullet points, or a list of citations. Return only the fields required by the supplied output schema.

Bill number: HB1733

<bill_text>
SENATE BILL 1774
 By Rose

 HOUSE BILL 1733

 By Moody

 AN ACT to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 37;
 Title 39, Chapter 17, Part 3; Title 40; Title 49 and
 Title 55, Chapter 10, Part 7, relative to
 harassment.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE STATE OF TENNESSEE:

 SECTION 1. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 39-17-308(e), is amended by

deleting subdivision (1) and substituting:

 (1) "Bullying" means an act committed by a school employee or student that

 substantially interferes with a victim's educational benefits, opportunities, or

 performance; and:

 (A) If the act takes place on school grounds, at any school-sponsored

 activity, on school-provided equipment or transportation, or at any official school

 bus stop, the act has the effect of:

 (i) Physically harming the victim or damaging the victim's

 property; or

 (ii) Knowingly placing the victim or victims in reasonable fear of

 physical harm to the victim or damage to the victim's property; or

 (B) If the act takes place off school property or outside of a school-

 sponsored activity, is directed specifically at a victim or victims and has the effect

 of creating a substantial disruption to the education environment or learning

 process;

 SECTION 2. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 39-17-308(e), is amended by adding

the following appropriately designated subdivisions:

 ( ) "School employee" means an employee of a private school, an LEA, a public

 charter school, or other public school;

 ( ) "Victim" means:

 (A) If the act is committed by a school employee, then any student; and

 (B) If the act is committed by a student, then another student;

 SECTION 3. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-6-4503(b)(3), is amended by

adding "and school employee" after "each student".

 SECTION 4. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-6-4503, is amended by adding

the following as a new subsection:

 (e) A teacher or school employee found to have committed an act of

 harassment, intimidation, bullying, or cyberbullying is subject to dismissal or suspension.

 SECTION 5. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-5-501(7), is amended by adding

the following as a new subdivision:

 (E) Committing an act of harassment, intimidation, bullying, or cyberbullying in

 violation of the school district's policy adopted in accordance with chapter 6, part 45 of

 this title;

 SECTION 6. This act takes effect July 1, 2026, the public welfare requiring it, and

applies to acts committed on or after that date.
</bill_text>

summary.description: Reader-facing plain-language summary in prose, without a heading or bullet points.

summary: This bill proposes changes to how bullying is defined and handled in schools. It redefines "bullying" as an act by a student or school employee that substantially interferes with a victim's educational benefits, opportunities, or performance. For acts on school grounds, sponsored activities, provided equipment, transportation, or official bus stops, the act must physically harm the victim or their property, or knowingly place them in reasonable fear of such harm. For acts occurring off school property or outside sponsored activities, the act must be directed at a victim and create a substantial disruption to the education environment or learning process. The bill defines "school employee" to include employees of private schools, public charter schools, other public schools, or local education agencies (LEAs). It defines a "victim" as any student if the act is committed by an employee, or another student if the act is committed by a student. Additionally, the bill would make teachers or school employees subject to suspension or dismissal if they commit acts of harassment, intimidation, bullying, or cyberbullying. It also adds the commission of such acts in violation of school district policy as a ground for certain actions under Tennessee Code Annotated Section 49-5-501. If passed, these changes would take effect July 1, 2026, and apply to acts committed on or after that date.
